name: tcrypt_header
description: Read a VeraCrypt or TrueCrypt volume header with cryptsetup's tcrypt mode, for a password (and, optionally, keyfiles) the case supplies. VeraCrypt and TrueCrypt leave no on-disk signature (crypto_id, identify/headers): this is the next reader once a candidate password exists. The password is read from `password_file` (a 0600 file; never a value on this tool's command line, in its environment, or in a file it writes) and given to `cryptsetup tcryptDump` on that program's own stdin. The answer says whether a header decrypted and, when it did, the header's non-secret fields from cryptsetup's own TCRYPT dump: version, driver requirement, flags, sector size, the master-key offset, the volume and hidden-volume sizes, the PBKDF and its hash, the cipher chain and mode, and the key size in bits; never the volume key, a salt, or any other derived secret. A header that does not decrypt is not proof the volume is not VeraCrypt or TrueCrypt: the password may be wrong, `header` may name the wrong region (normal, hidden or backup), or a keyfile may be missing. Only cryptsetup's exit 0 (a header decrypted) and exit 2 (no permission or bad passphrase) are answers about the password: status `complete`, `decrypted` true or false. Any other exit (1, 3, 4, a signal) answers `failed`, naming the exit code and saying nothing about the password, as does exit 0 with none of the header fields this tool reads. `password_file` must be mode 0600 (no access for group or other) or the call is refused. `pim` (VeraCrypt's Personal Iteration Multiplier) is refused, named: cryptsetup's --veracrypt-pim puts the number on its command line and --veracrypt-query-pim needs an interactive terminal, and whether a PIM may go on argv needs a decision this version does not have. `offset` is bytes, must be a multiple of 512 (cryptsetup's own --offset is in 512-byte sectors), and `source_kind: "device"` is required for a block device; a symbolic link, a FIFO or a socket named as `source` or a keyfile is refused. It refuses as JSON, before reading anything else (its own stdin included), when the call is not a job the harness ran as secret output (`SECRET_OUTPUT=1`); its manifest's `secret_output: "required"` makes every job of this tool one. It stops on SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP with one JSON answer and exit 128 + the signal, ending cryptsetup first; a read that has not returned after the tool's own clock and a grace period ends it with one partial answer (exit 0). A missing cryptsetup (macOS has none) answers `unavailable`, naming the program. A path shaped like a recovery password, an identifier or any other secret is withheld from every path this tool prints, by the shape rule its siblings carry. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 6: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape. It reports what cryptsetup printed on a pipe, so a host that cannot adopt orphans does not make an answer less than complete (`program_group` says so); a process cryptsetup (or its version probe) leaves behind is ended, and the answer is `partial` because a line it wrote to the pipe cannot be told from cryptsetup's. The answers after cryptsetup ran carry `program_group` (subreaper, left_behind, unproven, notes); a refusal, an error and `unavailable` do not.

source.description: The file or block device that may hold a VeraCrypt or TrueCrypt volume

source_kind.description: "file" (default) for a regular file, "device" for a block device; source must match, and a symbolic link is refused either way

password_file.description: A file holding the one candidate password this attempt tries (at most 4096 bytes; a trailing newline is dropped). Never a value given inline

keyfiles.description: Up to 16 keyfile paths, given to cryptsetup as --key-file; each must be a regular file, not a symbolic link

offset.description: Byte offset of the volume within source (default 0); must be a multiple of 512

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 60, 1 to 110; the manifest's timeout is 120)
